text: An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum of Elkosh.
The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD takes vengeance and is filled with wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his foes and holds his fury against his enemies.
The LORD is slow to anger but great in power; he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His way is in whirlwind and storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossom of Lebanon fades away.
The mountains quake before him, and the hills dissolve. The earth heaves at his presence, the world and all who live in it.
Who can stand before his fury? Who can endure the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before him.
The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; he knows those who take refuge in him.
But with a sweeping flood he will bring her place to an end, and he will pursue his enemies into darkness.

versions.text: But with an overwhelming flood he will make an end of her place, and he will pursue his enemies into darkness.
versions.explanation: "Make an end of her place" is awkward for oral reading and the antecedent of "her" is unclear. "Sweeping flood" better renders שֶׁטֶף עֹבֵר (a flood that passes through), and "bring her place to an end" flows more naturally while remaining literal. A footnote noting that "her" refers to Nineveh could help the listener.

text: Why do you scheme against the LORD? He himself will make an end of it; trouble will not rise up a second time.

versions.text: Whatever you plot against the LORD, he will bring to an end; trouble will not rise up a second time.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מַה־תְּחַשְּׁבוּן is a rhetorical question addressed to the plotters, not a concessive clause. Restoring the question form preserves the prophetic force and reads well aloud.

text: Though they are tangled together like thorns and soaked in their drink, they will be devoured like stubble, fully dry.

versions.text: Though they are tangled together like thorns and soaked in their drink, they will be devoured like stubble, dry and ready to burn.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew קַשׁ יָבֵשׁ מָלֵא means "fully dry stubble"; מָלֵא means "full/completely," not "ready to burn." The phrase "ready to burn" adds content not present in the text.

text: From you came the one who plots evil against the LORD, who counsels wickedness.
This is what the LORD says: Though they are strong and many, they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
Now I will break his yoke from your neck and tear your chains apart.

And this is what the LORD commands concerning you: Your name will have no offspring. I will cut off the carved image and the cast idol from the house of your gods. I will make your grave, for you are contemptible.
